atlas-se.0112: Programmes read name no sponsorship policy; the one published language rule is SEB’s, where some trainee roles require Swedish, so ask early whether the employer has hired from abroad.
atlas-se.0113: Posted vacancies: Arbetsförmedlingen’s Platsbanken, LinkedIn and employers’ own career pages; Invest in Gothenburg’s job portal filters English-speaking jobs, and Academic Work tags “Jobs in English”.
atlas-se.0114: Programmes: SEB, Swedbank, Volvo Group (search “Graduate” on its job site), Lantmännen and, for the state, the Ministry of Finance’s “Lediga jobb” page on regeringen.se.
atlas-se.0115: Fairs and services: KTH’s Armada and 14 other fairs, ARKAD at LTH in November, Chalmers Career Services with Unimeet Gothenburg, and Stockholm University’s career events and MyCareer profile.
atlas-se.0116: Missing the winter window: SEB’s intake closed on 11 January 2026 and runs only every other year; Swedbank’s reopens in January 2027.
atlas-se.0117: Writing a formal, long or boastful application: keep the CV to two pages or fewer, avoid superlatives, address the letter by first name and leave off your date of birth.
atlas-se.0118: Listing referees on the CV: provide references when asked, usually before a final offer.
atlas-se.0119: Relying only on posted jobs: many are filled through networking, so talk to alumni and guest speakers; asking strangers for a job in the first message works against you.
atlas-se.0120: Assuming English is enough everywhere: specific roles at SEB and most local employers need Swedish, and Swedish is common in informal workplace settings.
atlas-se.0121: SEB’s international trainee programme works in English but some roles require Swedish; Swedbank’s programme page names no language requirement, and neither names a certificate.
atlas-se.0122: Industrial groups such as Volvo and Lantmännen run programmes whose pages state no language requirement; Expat.com says English is widely used in international workplaces but Swedish is an advantage and in many roles a requirement.
atlas-se.0123: Gothenburg’s job portal filters English-speaking jobs, so many tech roles are open in English; list your Swedish level even for English-language roles to show commitment.
atlas-se.0124: The Ministry of Finance and Government Offices pages read name no English route; the state works in Swedish, so expect to need it.
atlas-se.0125: SSE’s 80% signed before graduation and 38% of international graduates staying in Sweden are the two figures read for the top business school; no source read gives a return-offer or conversion rate for Swedish internships or programmes.
atlas-se.0126: In 2025, 91.1% of recent tertiary graduates aged 20 to 34 were in work (EU 85.3%), while unemployment among 15-to-24-year-olds was 24.3%, so the entry problem is about age and network more than degree.
atlas-se.0127: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens work from day one with no permit, and since 2014 do not register with the Migration Agency.
atlas-se.0128: With a contract or programme of at least a year, register at a Skatteverket service office to get a personal identity number (personnummer); shorter stays get only a coordination number.
atlas-se.0129: A one-year master’s lasts about ten months, so it usually does not qualify for a personal number; a two-year master’s does.
atlas-se.0131: Pay the first tuition instalment before applying. Funds must sit in an account in your name only: parents’ sponsorship letters are refused.
atlas-se.0132: Since 11 June 2026 you may work 15 hours a week in term and full time in June, July and August; a credited internship of your degree is exempt from the cap.
atlas-se.0133: To renew, have 37.5 ECTS after the first year and 45 in each later year. With 30 Swedish credits you can switch to a work permit from inside Sweden.
atlas-se.0134: Non-EU students already holding a student permit in another EU country can come for up to 360 days within an EU mobility programme, on the university’s notification.
atlas-se.0136: SEK 10,656 a month (SEK 106,560 for ten months)
atlas-se.0137: Report your address to the Migration Agency within 30 days of arriving.
atlas-se.0139: For people completing a degree abroad or who graduated in the last two years: an internship agreement with a training plan, full health insurance and funds, for up to 18 months. Other internships count as ordinary employment, with its salary and union rules.
atlas-se.0141: Permit to look for work or start a business after studies
atlas-se.0142: After at least two semesters (60 ECTS) of higher education in Sweden, or a research project: 12 months (12 to 18 after a PhD), not renewable, with no limit on work.
atlas-se.0143: A qualifying job offer converts it from inside Sweden, and you can start as soon as the application is filed.
atlas-se.0146: Apply before your study permit expires: one day late and you are unlawfully present and lose the switch.
atlas-se.0148: The job must be advertised for 10 days on Platsbanken/EURES before the offer, the union consulted and Swedish collective terms met, with four insurances (health, life, work injury, occupational pension) from day one.
atlas-se.0149: The first permit is for up to two years and tied to employer and occupation; after four years of work permits in seven, permanent residence with a contract running at least 18 more months.
atlas-se.0150: Salary, from 16 June 2026 (90% of the median)
atlas-se.0152: Salary, shortage jobs and recent Swedish graduates (75%)
atlas-se.0154: A job not advertised for the 10 days cannot be fixed later: the application is refused.
atlas-se.0155: A contract of at least six months for highly qualified work and a three-year degree (180 ECTS) or five years of experience; the card lasts up to four years, and permanent residence comes after three.
atlas-se.0157: A hosting agreement with a research body approved by the Swedish Research Council; no work permit needed, up to four years, and short research stays from another EU country need no Swedish permit.
atlas-se.0158: Swedish PhD students are salaried employees with no tuition; four years of doctoral studies give permanent residence only with a job contract running at least 18 more months.
atlas-se.0160: SEK 1,500 (free for EU, Sida or Swedish Institute grants)
atlas-se.0161: Sweden has working-holiday agreements only with Australia, New Zealand, Canada, South Korea, Japan, Hong Kong, Argentina, Chile and Uruguay.
atlas-se.0162: For citizens of the partner countries aged 18 to 30 (35 for Canada, New Zealand and Australia), with SEK 15,000 and a return ticket: 12 months, and no switch to a work permit inside Sweden.
atlas-se.0163: Up to 90 days in any 180, with no employment; a permit cannot be applied for from inside Sweden after a visa-free or Schengen entry.
atlas-se.0165: 25% of pay is tax-free for seven years if you earn above the threshold and were not tax-resident in Sweden in the previous five years (study included); apply within three months of starting.
atlas-se.0168: Nothing to arrange in advance: you have a right of residence and may start work on your first day with no permit.
atlas-se.0169: After the Migration Agency’s decision, visa-required nationals collect the residence card at a Swedish embassy before travelling; visa-free nationals with a biometric passport (US, UK, Canada, Australia) can verify their identity in the Freja eID app and travel with the approval letter.
atlas-se.0170: In your first days, go in person to a government service centre (Statens servicecenter) with passport, a work or study contract of at least 12 months and your lease to register in the population register (folkbokföring). In practice it takes 8 to 16 weeks.
atlas-se.0171: One-year master’s programmes usually fall short of the 12 months, so students on them are often refused registration.
atlas-se.0172: None: you need no permit from the Migration Agency. Once registered and with a personal number, you can get a Swedish ID card (400 SEK).
atlas-se.0173: If you travelled with the approval letter, give your photo and fingerprints in Sweden to get the residence card (UT-kort).
atlas-se.0174: Staying 12 months or more you get a personal identity number (personnummer); for shorter stays, a coordination number (samordningsnummer) for tax.
atlas-se.0175: Ask the Tax Agency for a preliminary tax decision (A-skattsedel) at once, or your employer may withhold tax at the emergency rate.
atlas-se.0176: Register with the Social Insurance Agency (Försäkringskassan) to know which benefits you are covered for: work-based benefits such as sick pay apply from day one of a job.
atlas-se.0177: Without a personal number, for instance on an internship under a year, use your European Health Insurance Card or an S1 form.
atlas-se.0178: Students who pay tuition are covered by the state insurance FAS or FAS+ that their university takes out with Kammarkollegiet.
atlas-se.0179: Anyone lawfully resident in the EU has the right to a basic payment account (enkelt betalkonto) on a passport alone, even before the personal number: ask at SEB, Swedbank, Handelsbanken or Nordea with your employment letter.
atlas-se.0180: Until you have BankID, which needs the personal number and a Swedish ID card, use the Freja eID+ app, verified with your passport at a partner shop, for government portals.
atlas-se.0181: Keep your registered address true: a false registration of residence is a crime in Sweden.
atlas-se.0182: Apply to extend before your permit expires: you may then stay and keep working or studying on the same terms until the decision.
